answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers prove fake activity. At the market's nadir, when honest volume is thin, a gale of cheap fake identities would otherwise flood every listing; staking makes each fake account cost real money, so attackers run out of funds before they can dominate. Reputation then accrues only to staked identities, like ships tied to a wharf — anyone can see which ones have weathered real trade and which just appeared overnight.
